findings.severity: MEDIUM (disclosure; no code change required in this slice)
findings.title: An in-mount reconnect rejects the server's own hydration baseline, and the ref comment implies it cannot
findings.file: src/components/campaign/coop/CampaignCoopRouteSurfaceConnected.tsx:84-91 (the comment) and :131-145 (the effect whose dep array re-runs the connect)
findings.mechanism: The host effect's dep array is [campaignId, coopMode, matchId, roomCode, store]. A change to roomCode (invite rotation) or matchId re-runs the effect -- tearing down and reopening the transport -- WITHOUT unmounting the component, so the hostFold ref survives at whatever cursor it reached. The server hydrates every host (re)connection with buildBaselineEvent stamped sequence: -1 (CampaignSyncSession.ts:779), which foldCampaignFrame pins to cursor 0 (campaignAuthoritativeFold.ts:118-121), and foldCampaignSnapshot then rejects it because `adopted (0) < fold.lastSequence` (campaignAuthoritativeFold.ts:74-76). The baseline -- which is precisely what carries the commits that landed during the socket gap -- is dropped, and the live tail resumes on top of a fold that is missing them.
findings.proof: PROBE-1: a reviewer-added row mounting a host, folding to cursor 7, re-rendering with a rotated room code, then emitting a baseline at revision 9 carrying balance 123456. Result: Expected 123456, Received 700000 -- the baseline was rejected. Probe reverted; worktree clean.
findings.whyItMatters: The ref comment at :84-91 explains the ref choice by describing this exact hazard ('one that came back quoting a cursor past that baseline's own sequence: -1 would REJECT its own hydration frame and backfill nothing') and implies the ref avoids it. The ref avoids it only across REMOUNTS. Within a mount the hazard is live, and H2 is what makes the reconnect quote a cursor at all. In a slice whose entire purpose is curing host-view staleness, a residual path that silently re-introduces staleness must be named.
findings.notARegression: Correct -- before this slice the host never updated at all, so this is a narrowing of the defect, not a widening. Probability is low (the gap is the GM's own socket reopen, and the GM is the party committing). This is why the required edit is disclosure, not a code fix: the candidate fixes (resetting the fold on effect re-run, which would defeat H2; or making a sequence:-1 baseline an unconditional replace, which changes shared GUEST semantics) are both out of this slice's scope and would need their own red-first row.
findings.relationToTheReceipt: The receipt's nonClaims already disclose the same adopt-at-0 rule as a pre-existing hazard FOR GUESTS ('a guest holding a cursor above 0 would reject a large-gap resync baseline ... is UNCHANGED by this slice'). It does not disclose that the host now has an instance of it. That asymmetry is the gap.

findings.title: H2's stated D9 justification is not supported by the server routing
findings.file: src/components/campaign/coop/CampaignCoopRouteSurfaceConnected.tsx:138-144 (comment) and the H1+H2 commit message body
findings.claimAsWritten: 'it matters for the D9 case - a GM connecting from ANOTHER device is not the registered host and is routed down the same cursor-resumable replica path a guest takes.'
findings.measured: No arm reachable from this component's HOST effect consumes envelope.lastSeq. (a) If the second device's verified principal matches entry.hostPlayerId it takes the host arm (bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:947-1018) -- unconditional joinMember, cursor never read. (b) If it does not, the next arm is the membership-active rejoin at :1022-1040 -- also an unconditional joinMember, cursor never read. (c) Next is the grant/replica route handleRoomCodeGuestJoin at :1099 -- `grep -n lastSeq src/lib/multiplayer/server/handleRoomCodeGuestJoin.ts` returns NOTHING. (d) Only then comes the :1082 lastSeq arm, whose own comment at :1091-1093 says it 'is only reached when the grant/replica route fell back (for example explicit unavailable adapters)'. Separately, a GM whose local campaign record says mode 'guest' never reaches this effect at all -- the guest effect handles them, and it threaded lastSeq before this slice.
findings.alsoTrue: H2 is inert on the wire even in the arm it could reach, on a cold connect: campaignSyncTransport.ts:215 emits `...(lastSeq >= 0 ? { lastSeq } : {})`, and hostFold starts at lastSequence -1, so a fresh mount sends no cursor at all. H2's only live effect is on an in-mount effect re-run -- the same path as F-R1.
findings.assessment: H2 is harmless, is pinned by a discriminating test row (M2), and is defensible as role symmetry and as forward-preparation for the cutover. The code is fine; only the justification overstates. Correct the comment rather than remove the cursor.
findings.explicitlyNotDisputed: The receipt's own F1 already concedes 'For a GM who IS the registered host, H2 changes nothing on the wire' and the nonClaims say 'H2 is NOT claimed to fix host reconnect backfill'. The claim discipline is good; it is the one remaining positive justification that does not hold.

findings.title: The mirror-store refactor adds two spurious zustand notifications
findings.detail: Before the refactor, applySnapshot returned EARLY -- before calling set() -- when the frame was not a CampaignSnapshotPublished or failed to parse. Those two guards now live inside foldCampaignSnapshot, so set() is entered and the reducer returns {}. I verified against the repo's zustand (5.0.8) that `set(() => ({}))` DOES notify subscribers: two no-op sets produced 2 listener notifications.
findings.impact: None observable. `grep -rn 'useCampaignMirrorStore.subscribe' src` returns no call sites, so the only subscribers are React selector hooks, which compare the selected slice with Object.is and will not re-render. Recorded for completeness because it is a real behavioral delta the receipt does not mention, not because it needs fixing.

findings.title: The host effect gained a !campaignId guard that is practically unreachable
findings.detail: The guard widened from `coopMode !== 'host' || !matchId || !roomCode` to include `|| !campaignId`. Since campaignId = campaign?.id and coopMode = campaign?.coopSession?.mode, a null campaign already fails the coopMode check, so the new clause can only fire on an empty-string id. It mirrors the guest effect's existing guard (:231) and is needed for the type narrowing the projection call requires. No reachable behavior change; the refusal/audit/pending UI is not lost in any realistic state.
findings.alsoChecked: `store` was added to the dep array. useCampaignStore() returns a module-level singleton (src/stores/campaign/useCampaignStore.ts:168-185, `campaignStoreInstance` memoized), so the reference is stable and the added dep causes no reconnect churn.

findings.title: Test quality is high and the suite is genuinely discriminating
findings.detail: The suite drives the REAL component and the real frame decoders -- jest.requireActual keeps campaignEventFromMessage, parseCampaignCoopSnapshot and applyCampaignEvent live and fakes only connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport (test file :52-57), with openCoopRuntimeSession/subscribeCoopPendingProposals stubbed (:62-69) so the rows stay on the view side. Every row is pinned by at least one mutant, no row is redundant (M1/M2/M3 each kill a distinct set), and the single-player row is a genuine negative control (asserts connectMock was never called). The parity row's limitation -- it cannot catch symmetric breakage, as M4 showed -- is inherent to parity assertions, not a defect.
